hero.headline: US conducts second round of strikes on Iran in three days
hero.body:
The United States carried out fresh military strikes against Iranian targets, marking the second such action within three days. The strikes occurred while both nations maintain a fragile ceasefire and continue diplomatic negotiations aimed at ending a three-month conflict.

President Trump stated that Iran is "negotiating on fumes" following the latest military action. According to U.S. officials, the new strikes were conducted in response to Iranian attack drones that U.S. forces had previously downed.

Iran responded to the American strikes by targeting a U.S. airbase. This exchange of military fire has tested the durability of the ceasefire agreement that both sides have been attempting to maintain while pursuing peace talks.

The renewed hostilities have triggered significant reactions in global financial markets. Oil prices jumped 3 percent after Iran announced its strike on U.S. forces. Asian stock markets declined as investors assessed mixed signals from the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict.

The situation has created broader pressure on the Trump administration regarding the war. The president expressed indifference to midterm political considerations, suggesting that domestic electoral concerns would not influence his approach to the conflict.

The three-month war has now entered a particularly unstable phase, with both military operations and diplomatic efforts proceeding simultaneously. The ceasefire remains technically in place despite the exchange of strikes, though its fragility has become increasingly evident.

Neither country has indicated plans to completely abandon the negotiating process, even as military operations continue. Both governments face the challenge of pursuing meaningful diplomatic talks while managing domestic and international pressure following the renewed military engagement.

Analysts and officials have emphasized the critical importance of safeguarding international maritime routes to ensure the uninterrupted flow of energy. Iran's effective closure of the strait of Hormuz has severely constrained global oil distribution. The narrow waterway typically handles approximately 100 tankers daily, with roughly 20 percent of the world's total crude oil passing through this vital trade route.

The conflict has resulted in substantial damage to Middle Eastern oil infrastructure. Iranian and Israeli military operations have struck petrochemical plants and production facilities across the region, disrupting energy supplies significantly.

The price of Brent crude has soared dramatically since the start of the year, rising more than 50 percent and hitting a peak of 119.50 dollars per barrel in March. Current trading prices remain around 109 dollars per barrel.

These elevated energy costs have directly impacted consumers globally. In the United States, average fuel prices recently passed 4 dollars per gallon for the first time in four years, while UK motorists have also faced substantially higher petrol and diesel prices.

The latest strikes mark an escalation in tensions following the initial ceasefire announcement. Both governments now face mounting pressure to manage renewed military engagement while continuing their pursuit of a diplomatic resolution to the conflict.

cards.headline: Israel orders evacuation of southern Lebanon, begins strikes
cards.teaser: The Israeli military declared areas south of the Zahrani River combat zones and issued evacuation orders.
cards.body:
Israel has designated areas south of the Zahrani River as combat zones and issued evacuation orders for residents in southern Lebanon, including the city of Tyre. The military subsequently launched strikes in the newly designated combat zones.

The action marks a significant escalation of military operations in southern Lebanon, with Israeli forces conducting fresh strikes following the evacuation warnings.

cards.headline: Kuwait reports missile and drone attack amid Iran war
cards.teaser: Kuwait said it faced a missile and drone attack as the regional ceasefire faces new challenges.
cards.body:
Kuwait reported coming under missile and drone attack, adding another security challenge to an already unstable region. The attack occurred as the ceasefire in the Iran war continues to face repeated violations.

The incident in Kuwait represents a widening of security concerns beyond the direct US-Iran conflict. The attack came during the same period as renewed US strikes on Iranian targets.

cards.headline: Oil prices rise after US attacks on Iran
cards.teaser: Oil markets reacted to renewed US military strikes on Iranian targets.
cards.body:
Oil prices jumped following US strikes on Iranian targets, marking the second attack in three days. The strikes targeted attack drones and a drone ground-control station, conducted as self-defense measures according to US officials.

The military action threatens the fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran, which are currently engaged in peace negotiations to end the three-month conflict. Market concerns about supply disruptions and the stability of ongoing talks have driven the price increases amid continued hostilities.

cards.headline: Internet access returns to Iran after monthslong shutdown with heavy restrictions
cards.teaser: Iranians regained internet service after authorities ended a shutdown lasting several months, though users report slow speeds and blocked access to major apps.
cards.body:
Iranian authorities have restored internet access following a prolonged shutdown. Users reported experiencing slow and unreliable connections in various regions as service came back online.

Major platforms including YouTube and Instagram remain heavily restricted under the renewed internet access. The restoration marks the end of a monthslong period without connectivity for Iranian citizens.

cards.headline: Zelensky urges Trump and Congress to provide Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president asked for anti-missile defense systems, acknowledging Ukraine has not built its own production capability for such weapons.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and members of Congress to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia. Zelensky said Ukraine has achieved success in defending against drones but has not built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.

The Ukrainian leader made his appeal directly to American leadership, highlighting the gap in Ukraine's defensive capabilities. While the country has developed effective drone defenses, it lacks

hero.headline: Uganda closes border with Congo as Ebola cases reach capital
hero.teaser: Uganda shut its border with Congo after seven Ebola cases were confirmed in Kampala.
hero.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo following confirmed Ebola cases in the capital, Kampala. Seven cases have been reported in the city as authorities work to contain the outbreak.

The DRC's outbreak in the east of the country has grown significantly, with over 900 suspected cases and 119 suspected deaths reported. The WHO has assessed the outbreak as posing a very high risk to the country, though the risk of global spread remains low. Uganda has implemented disease surveillance systems to monitor and respond to the virus.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over chemical contamination
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed its largest ever lawsuit against the US company over firefighting foam.
cards.body:
Australia has launched a record-breaking legal action against 3M, seeking over $2 billion in damages for contamination caused by "forever chemicals" in firefighting foam. The lawsuit, filed by the federal government, represents the largest legal claim the country has ever brought and centers on contamination at defense bases.

The case focuses on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), chemicals used in firefighting foam at military installations across Australia. Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the action against the US multinational manufacturer, with the damages sought reflecting the extent of contamination and cleanup costs at affected defense sites.

cards.headline: Australia charges woman with joining Islamic State after Syria return
cards.teaser: A woman who returned from Syria faces charges related to membership in the terrorist group.
cards.body:
Australian authorities have charged a woman with joining Islamic State following her return from Syria. She was among several groups of women and children who spent years in a Syrian camp before being repatriated to Australia in recent months.

The woman now faces criminal charges related to her involvement with the extremist group. Her case is part of a broader pattern of Australian citizens and their families being brought back from Syrian detention camps.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady described being frightened by her husband's debate performance against Trump.
cards.body:
In a CBS News interview set to air Sunday, former first lady Jill Biden said she was "frightened" while watching her husband's debate performance against Donald Trump. She stated she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since.

The comments reveal the Biden family's immediate reaction to the debate, which proved to be a pivotal moment in the 2024 election campaign.

cards.headline: Former CIA official charged with stealing more than $40 million in gold bars
cards.teaser: A former senior CIA official with top secret clearance is accused of stealing hundreds of gold bars from the federal government and hiding them in his home.
cards.body:
A former senior CIA official with top secret-level clearance has been charged with stealing hundreds of gold bars worth more than $40 million from the federal government. Investigators say the official kept the stolen gold bars hidden in his home.

The case represents one of the most significant theft allegations involving a former intelligence community member in recent years.

cards.headline: California governor announces plan for 100 percent tax on Justice Department fund payouts
cards.teaser: Governor Newsom said California will impose a full tax on payments from the DOJ Anti-Weaponization Fund, a $1.8 billion program established by the Trump administration.
cards.body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom announced plans to impose a 100 percent tax on payments that state residents receive from the Department of Justice's "Anti-Weaponization Fund." The $1.776 billion fund was created by the Trump administration in May to compensate what it describes as victims of "lawfare and weaponization."

The move represents an effort by Newsom to counteract the federal program through state taxation. A similar proposal has been introduced by a New York state lawmaker targeting residents who receive payouts from the fund.

cards.headline: Former federal judges request reopening of Trump IRS lawsuit to investigate settlement
cards.teaser: A group of former federal judges has asked a court to reopen a lawsuit involving Trump and the IRS, calling for an investigation into the payout fund created by the settlement.
cards.body:
Former federal judges have filed a motion urging a court to reopen a lawsuit between Donald Trump and the Internal Revenue Service. The former judges are requesting an investigation into a fund established as part of the settlement, which they have described as potentially fraudulent.

The former judges characterized the Trump anti-weaponization fund as unprecedentedly fraudulent in their court filing. They argue the settlement and its associated payout mechanism warrant judicial scrutiny and a potential fraud probe.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared husband was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump during the 2024 presidential campaign.
cards.body:
Former First Lady Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened while watching Joe Biden's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. She said she thought her husband might have suffered a stroke, describing his faltering performance as unlike anything she had witnessed before or since.

Biden's comments came in an interview with CBS News set to air on Sunday. Her recollection highlighted the significant concern surrounding the debate, which became a pivotal moment during the 2024 presidential campaign.

cards.headline: Becerra takes lead in California governor race ahead of June primary
cards.teaser: A new poll shows Xavier Becerra opening a lead in the race to succeed Gavin Newsom as California governor, with the primary election approaching.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra has moved ahead in polling for the California gubernatorial race as the state prepares for its June primary election. Becerra is competing to replace Governor Gavin Newsom, who cannot seek another term.

The race features multiple Democratic candidates vying for the nomination. California Democrats face a packed field of choices as the primary election nears, with the contest shifting rapidly according to recent polling data.

cards.headline: Internet access returns to Iran after monthslong shutdown with heavy restrictions
cards.teaser: Iranians regained internet service after authorities ended a shutdown lasting several months, though users report slow speeds and blocked access to major apps.
cards.body:
Iranian authorities have restored internet access following a prolonged shutdown. Users reported experiencing slow and unreliable connections in various regions as service came back online.

Major platforms including YouTube and Instagram remain heavily restricted under the renewed internet access. The restoration marks the end of a monthslong period without connectivity for Iranian citizens.

hero.headline: Google employee charged with using company data for $1.2 million in bets
hero.teaser: A longtime Google worker faces insider trading charges for allegedly using internal information to profit on prediction markets.
hero.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York have charged Michele Spagnuolo, a Google information security engineer, with fraud for allegedly using confidential company data to profit on Polymarket, a prediction betting platform. Spagnuolo made approximately $1.2 million through bets related to Google search trends in 2025.

Prosecutors allege that Spagnuolo accessed Google's confidential information to gain an unfair advantage, knowing the outcomes of his wagers before the general trading public. This marks the second known federal case involving criminal charges against someone accused of using insider information to make substantial profits on a prediction market site.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over contamination at defense sites
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed its largest lawsuit ever against the US manufacturer over alleged pollution from firefighting foam.
cards.body:
Australia's federal government has launched legal action against 3M, seeking damages exceeding A$2 billion for contamination at defense bases. Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the case, which represents the largest lawsuit the government has ever brought against a private company.

The lawsuit centers on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—known as "forever chemicals"—found in firefighting foam used at military installations. These persistent compounds have contaminated multiple defense sites across the country.

cards.headline: Pork prices in China hit 16-year low amid weak consumer spending
cards.teaser: A key inflation indicator dropped to its lowest level since 2010 as oversupply and sluggish demand weigh on the economy.
cards.body:
Pork prices in China have fallen to their lowest level in 16 years, signaling economic weakness in the world's second-largest economy. The decline reflects sluggish consumer spending and an oversupply of hogs in the market.

Pork is a key inflation indicator in China, where it forms a dietary staple. The sharp price drop underscores how Chinese households remain hesitant to spend despite government stimulus efforts. Farmers had ramped up production in recent years, flooding the market with supply and pushing prices down.

cards.headline: Trump administration in talks to fund US drone manufacturers
cards.teaser: The White House is discussing financial support for American drone companies as Pentagon spending in the sector increases.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is discussing potential funding for US drone manufacturers, according to reports from the Wall Street Journal and Reuters. The talks reflect growing Pentagon investment in unmanned aerial systems as defense officials prioritize drone technology for military operations.

The proposed support aims to strengthen domestic drone production and reduce dependence on foreign suppliers. Multiple US companies in the unmanned systems sector are involved in these discussions.

cards.headline: China expands factory construction abroad as trade surplus grows
cards.teaser: Chinese manufacturers are building production facilities in other countries, raising concerns among competitors.
cards.body:
China is accelerating the construction of manufacturing facilities outside its borders as its global trade surplus continues to expand. The outward shift of production capacity has drawn attention from international competitors worried about market share.

Chinese companies are establishing factories in multiple countries as part of a strategy to maintain export access and navigate trade barriers. The expansion comes as China's trade surplus with the rest of the world has grown substantially. Industry observers note the trend could reshape global manufacturing patterns and supply chains.

cards.headline: Coffee prices reach $5 at city outlets amid global supply pressures
cards.teaser: Urban coffee shops are charging $5 per cup as tariffs, climate factors, and shifting consumer tastes affect pricing.
cards.body:
Coffee prices have climbed to £5 at some city centre outlets, driven by a combination of global economic forces. Tariffs, climate conditions, and shifting consumer preferences have all contributed to the surge in retail prices.

The market dynamics reflect broader economic pressures on the coffee trade. Younger consumers' demand for specialty coffee products, alongside climate impacts on supply and trade policy effects, have converged to push prices higher in urban markets.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey investigate FIFA over World Cup ticket sales
cards.teaser: State authorities are examining whether fans were misled about ticket prices and seating for upcoming matches.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The probe focuses on matches scheduled for MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, and was announced by New York Attorney General Letitia James and New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport.

The investigation examines complaints from fans who say they were misled about seat locations and claims that FIFA's public messaging about tickets contributed to inflated prices. A subpoena has been issued seeking information about FIFA's ticket sales and marketing practices.

hero.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over contamination at defense sites
hero.body:
The Australian government has filed a lawsuit against US manufacturing giant 3M over alleged contamination from firefighting foam at defense installations. The case seeks damages of A$2 billion, marking the largest legal action ever brought by the Australian government.

The lawsuit centers on the use of firefighting foam containing so-called forever chemicals at military and defense sites across Australia. These chemicals, known as PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances), persist in the environment and have raised health and environmental concerns.

3M manufactured firefighting foams used at Australian defense facilities over several decades. The company has faced similar litigation in other countries over PFAS contamination from its products.

The Australian case represents an escalation in government action against manufacturers of PFAS-containing products. The chemicals have been detected in soil and groundwater at numerous defense bases and firefighting training areas.

Forever chemicals earn their nickname because they do not break down naturally in the environment. They accumulate over time and can enter drinking water supplies and the food chain.

The A$2 billion figure reflects the government's estimated costs for cleanup and remediation at affected defense sites. Australia operates military installations across the continent, many of which used firefighting foams for training and emergency response.

3M announced in 2022 that it would stop producing PFAS chemicals by the end of 2025. The company has set aside billions of dollars to address PFAS-related claims globally.

The Australian lawsuit follows years of testing and investigation at defense sites. Environmental regulators have documented PFAS contamination at locations where firefighting foam was regularly deployed.

The case will proceed through Australian courts. The government has not disclosed a timeline for resolution, though complex environmental litigation typically takes years to conclude.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading over Polymarket bets
cards.teaser: A Google engineer faces charges after allegedly making $1.2 million on Polymarket wagers related to internal company information.
cards.body:
Federal authorities have charged a Google engineer with insider trading for allegedly using confidential company information to make profitable bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The engineer made over $1.2 million through wagers related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign.

According to the complaint, the engineer wagered more than $2.7 million across multiple bets using knowledge gained from their position at the company. This marks the second known case in which the federal government has filed criminal charges against someone for allegedly exploiting insider information to profit on a prediction market site.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: The Psyche spacecraft sent back high-resolution photographs of Mars during a recent pass by the planet.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche mission has transmitted striking images of Mars captured during a flyby of the red planet. The spacecraft photographed Mars while traveling toward its destination, a metal-rich asteroid in the outer solar system.

The images include detailed views of Mars' south polar region. Psyche used the planetary encounter to test its imaging systems while taking advantage of the close approach to capture unique perspectives of Mars.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 SUVs
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker will begin customer deliveries of its R2 model next month.
cards.body:
Rivian has announced June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of its R2 SUV. CEO RJ Scaringe has called the vehicle "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date," signaling its significance for the company's future.

The R2 marks an important expansion for the electric vehicle manufacturer as it moves beyond its initial R1T truck and R1S SUV offerings.

cards.headline: Scientists achieve perfect randomness using quantum mechanics
cards.teaser: Researchers have generated truly random numbers for the first time using quantum computing systems.
cards.body:
Scientists have produced perfect randomness through quantum mechanical processes, a breakthrough in random number generation. The research demonstrates that quantum systems can create numbers that are truly unpredictable rather than merely appearing random.

The achievement has implications for cryptography and data security. Perfect random numbers could strengthen encryption methods used to protect sensitive information, as they eliminate patterns that could be exploited by adversaries.

cards.headline: National Trust applies 17 tonnes of chalk to restore hillside figure
cards.teaser: Staff and volunteers will restore a famous chalk figure to prevent it from fading in the rain.
cards.body:
The National Trust is applying 17 tonnes of fresh chalk to restore a famous hillside figure in the UK. The restoration project involves staff and volunteers working together to refresh the chalk outline of the well-known landmark.

Rain has caused the original chalk to fade over time, making the restoration work necessary to preserve the site and prevent further deterioration from weather exposure.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer center AI platform
cards.teaser: The oncology AI company secured Series B funding led by Battery Ventures.
cards.body:
Triomics has closed a $22 million Series B funding round to develop artificial intelligence tools designed specifically for cancer treatment centers. Battery Ventures led the investment round.

The company focuses on creating AI applications tailored to oncology practices. The funding will support development of tools aimed at cancer centers and their specific operational needs.

hero.headline: Crystal Palace wins first European trophy with Conference League final victory
hero.body:
Crystal Palace claimed their maiden European title by defeating Rayo Vallecano in the Conference League final in Leipzig, with Jean-Philippe Mateta scoring the decisive goal.

The victory represents a historic moment for the club. As the 15th-placed finishers in the Premier League, Palace would not have qualified for European football next season without this triumph. The Conference League win automatically secures their spot in the Europa League, a competition neither finalist would have accessed through their domestic league positions.

Oliver Glasner managed Palace to the trophy in his final match in charge before departing the club. The manager reflected on the achievement by stating that Palace now belongs in the Europa League, the level where the club should be competing. His 12-month tenure included this remarkable trophy win that caps a successful period at Selhurst Park.

Club chairman Steve Parish witnessed the occasion alongside UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin. Parish has overseen Palace's journey from near extinction 16 years ago to European champions. The chairman's presence at this moment underscores the significance of the achievement for the organization.

Mateta's goal came after his own turbulent path to the club. The striker's move to Milan was abandoned following a failed medical, making his match-winning performance particularly poignant. His introduction from the bench provided Palace with renewed impetus in their push for victory.

The triumph grants Palace entry to the Europa League following their exclusion from the competition last season. As holders of the FA Cup, Palace had been denied European football due to breaches of multi-club ownership rules. This Conference League victory provides redemption and delivers the continental football the club was previously denied.

For Rayo Vallecano, the loss represents a missed opportunity. The Spanish side, who finished eighth in their domestic league, reached the final but could not overcome Palace's performance. European football through the Conference League offered both clubs a pathway to next season's Europa League that their league positions would not otherwise have provided.

The final capped an exhausting campaign for Palace's squad. Multiple players accumulated over 4,000 minutes throughout the season, with Maxence Lacroix among those who logged extensive playing time. This workload preceded the European final, making Glasner's decision to field a strong team a significant commitment to the trophy.

Palace secured their place in the top flight for a 14th consecutive season with this result. The Conference League victory ensures the club's Premier League status while also delivering continental football and European revenue for the upcoming campaign.

Glasner's full-length dive on the pitch following the final whistle reflected the magnitude of the achievement. His tenure at Palace will now be defined by this historic European trophy, cementing his legacy at the club despite his departure.

cards.headline: Packers running back Josh Jacobs released from jail as prosecutor reviews charges
cards.teaser: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was released from police custody as the district attorney continues to review the case.
cards.body:
Packers running back Josh Jacobs was released from jail Wednesday following his arrest on five charges, including felony strangulation and domestic violence offenses.

The district attorney is currently reviewing the case to determine next steps. Head coach Matt LaFleur has not commented on the situation.

cards.headline: Senators Cruz and Cantwell introduce bipartisan college sports reform bill
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell have introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at reforming college sports.
cards.body:
The proposed bill addresses multiple aspects of college athletics, including a salary cap and transfer limits for student athletes. The legislation targets issues such as coach poaching, following recent high-profile moves like Lane Kiffin's jump to LSU.

The bill, called the Protect College Sports Act, includes provisions for transfer and eligibility rules as well as cap enforcement mechanisms. SEC leaders are discussing contingency plans as the legislation moves through Congress.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey subpoena FIFA over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey have issued subpoenas to FIFA as part of an investigation into World Cup ticket sales.
cards.body:
New York and New Jersey's attorneys general have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup, with a specific focus on matches at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford. The subpoena seeks information about FIFA's ticket sales and pricing structures.

The investigation centers on fan complaints that they were misled about seat locations. Attorneys general Letitia James and Jennifer Davenport are also examining whether FIFA's public messaging around ticket availability has contributed to inflated prices throughout the tournament.

cards.headline: Georgia coach Kirby Smart says he would support SEC leaving NCAA
cards.teaser: University of Georgia head football coach Kirby Smart suggested the SEC could break away from the NCAA.
cards.body:
Georgia football coach Kirby Smart has indicated openness to the SEC operating independently from the NCAA. His comments reflect ongoing discussions about the conference's future structure amid broader changes in college athletics.

The potential departure would represent a significant shift, as the SEC has long operated within NCAA governance. Smart's position adds to the debate among college athletics stakeholders about whether conferences should break away to establish their own regulatory frameworks.

cards.headline: Dodgers place Kiké Hernández on injured list with oblique tear
cards.teaser: Los Angeles Dodgers utility player Enrique 'Kiké' Hernández returned to the injured list after being diagnosed with an oblique tear.
cards.body:
Hernández suffered a significant tear in his left oblique. The injury occurred just two games after the Dodgers activated him for his season debut.

The team recalled Alex Freeland from Triple-A to fill the roster spot. The Dodgers had avoided placing Max Muncy on the injured list when they initially activated Hernández.

cards.headline: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson calls coaching changes a breath of fresh air
cards.teaser: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson described the team's offseason coaching changes positively.
cards.body:
Jackson said the changes feel like a breath of fresh air for the organization. He also stated his love for the Ravens has never wavered.

Jackson said he plans to leave the conversation about a fully guaranteed contract in the past. He stayed quiet on current contract negotiations during organized team activities.

hero.headline: Spielberg Says Hollywood Should Never Use AI as Final Word on Creative Decisions
hero.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against artificial intelligence taking over creative processes in filmmaking during an appearance on the IMO podcast hosted by Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson.

The director said he sees value in AI for solving medical problems but opposes its use as a replacement for human creativity in Hollywood. Spielberg said he does not want AI taking over the creative process in the film industry.

He drew a clear boundary on where he believes the technology belongs in entertainment. Spielberg said he draws the line at allowing AI to serve as the final word on anything creative.

The comments reflect ongoing debate in the entertainment industry about the role of artificial intelligence in filmmaking. Studios and creators continue to grapple with how emerging technologies should be integrated into production while preserving human artistic control.

Spielberg has directed some of the most successful films in cinema history, including Jaws, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, and Schindler's List. His views carry weight in an industry navigating rapid technological change.

The podcast appearance comes as Hollywood unions and studios negotiate contract terms addressing AI use in production. Writers and actors struck in 2023 partly over concerns about artificial intelligence replacing human work.

Spielberg's position aligns with many creatives who argue that while AI can assist with technical tasks, human judgment should remain central to artistic decisions. The director specifically distinguished between beneficial medical applications of the technology and what he sees as inappropriate use in creative fields.

The entertainment industry continues to explore AI applications ranging from visual effects to script analysis, but questions remain about appropriate boundaries for the technology in creative work.

cards.headline: ABC World News Tonight Wins Fourth Straight Emmy for Outstanding Live News Program
cards.teaser: ABC News led the 47th annual News Emmy Awards with eight wins, while National Geographic took seven awards.
cards.body:
ABC World News Tonight With David Muir claimed the outstanding live news program award at the 47th annual News Emmy Awards, marking its fourth consecutive win in the category.

ABC News dominated the ceremony with eight total Emmy wins. National Geographic earned seven awards, with multiple recognitions for the series Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller. Both networks are Disney subsidiaries.

cards.headline: Student Journalist Criticizes CBS News During Emmy Acceptance Speech
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos, a high school senior, called out CBS News while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior from District of Columbia International School in Washington, used his acceptance speech for the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards to critique CBS News, saying its recent direction undermines the legacy of the legendary journalist the award honors.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the annual scholarship, which recognizes outstanding student journalists. Campos's remarks came as CBS News faces scrutiny over editorial decisions, including the non-renewal of 60 Minutes correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi's contract following disputes over editorial control of her reporting.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Responds to Criticism Over Recent Outfits
cards.teaser: The singer addressed backlash over her recent wardrobe choices, saying women should not be responsible for how men sexualize them.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo responded to internet criticism of her recent clothing choices. The singer faced accusations that her outfits both infantilized and sexualized her.

Rodrigo said women should not be responsible for some guy sexualizing them. The comments came after online commenters posted critical reactions to her recent appearances.

cards.headline: Morris Day Denies Participation in Freedom 250 Concert Despite Being Listed in Lineup
cards.teaser: The musician said he and the Time will not perform at a National Mall concert next month, contradicting official announcements.
cards.body:
Morris Day has denied rumors that he and the Time will perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for the National Mall next month, stating "It's a no for me" regarding the event.

Despite Day's denial, organizers had officially announced him as a headliner for a show on June 27 as part of a 16-day patriotic fair in Washington. The announcement drew pushback from fans, prompting Day's public clarification about his non-participation in the controversial event.

cards.headline: Jimmy Kimmel Honors Adam Carolla at Hollywood Walk of Fame Ceremony
cards.teaser: The late-night host delivered an emotional speech calling Carolla his life partner at the podcaster's Walk of Fame star unveiling.
cards.body:
Jimmy Kimmel became emotional while speaking at Adam Carolla's Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony on Wednesday. Kimmel called the podcaster and comedian his "life partner," noting that if the comment sounds gay, it was and it is.

The two met in 1994 while working together on Kevin and Bean, a Los Angeles radio show. Their friendship and professional relationship has continued since those early radio days.

hero.headline: DOJ opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
hero.body:
The Trump administration has launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to reports from CNN and the New York Times.

Prosecutors are examining whether Carroll, 82, committed perjury during a 2022 deposition in her civil lawsuits against Trump. In that deposition, Carroll stated she had not accepted outside financial support for her legal battles. However, approximately six months later, before trial proceedings began, Carroll's attorneys disclosed to the judge and Trump's legal team that a nonprofit funded by Reid Hoffman, the billionaire LinkedIn co-founder, had paid some of her legal fees and expenses.

Trump's lawyers argued that Carroll concealed Hoffman's financial backing and that this concealment undermined her credibility in the case. Carroll's legal representatives countered that she never met or spoke with anyone from the nonprofit organization. Following this disclosure, Trump's attorney Alina Habba was permitted to conduct a second deposition with Carroll to address the funding issue.

In 2024, a three-judge federal appeals court panel in New York dismissed claims that Carroll had committed perjury in her initial deposition.

Carroll, a longtime advice columnist, first made her allegations public in her 2019 book "What Do We Need Men For?" She claimed Trump assaulted her in a New York department store dressing room. Trump has denied the allegations, stating Carroll was "totally lying" and was "not my type."

Carroll's legal battles against Trump have already resulted in significant outcomes. A jury found Trump liable for sexual abuse and defamation, awarding Carroll five million dollars in damages. A separate jury subsequently ordered Trump to pay eighty-three million dollars in a related defamation case. Trump has appealed both judgments.

Todd Blanche, the acting attorney general, has recused himself from the Justice Department investigation due to his prior role representing Trump in Carroll's civil cases.

The investigation represents the latest in a series of criminal inquiries initiated by Trump's Justice Department into political opponents. Federal prosecutors have also investigated former FBI Director James Comey, New York Attorney General Letitia James, and Democratic members of Congress including Adam Schiff and Ilhan Omar. None of these investigations have resulted in criminal convictions to date.

Neither the Justice Department nor Carroll's legal representatives provided immediate comment on the investigation.

cards.headline: US military strikes Iranian drone site after intercepting four attack drones
cards.teaser: American forces shot down four Iranian one-way attack drones and destroyed a ground control station preparing to launch a fifth.
cards.body:
The US military intercepted four Iranian attack drones in the Strait of Hormuz and struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone. The drones posed a threat to a commercial vessel in the strait, according to US Central Command.

The military action represents the second confrontation between the US and Iran in 48 hours. It occurred amid ongoing negotiations to end the three-month war, during what has been described as a fragile ceasefire between the two countries.

cards.headline: Former federal judges ask court to reopen Trump's IRS lawsuit over settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former judges argues the Trump administration circumvented the court by negotiating a settlement creating a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A group of former federal judges asked a federal court to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. The judges argue the administration bypassed the court by negotiating a settlement with the president and establishing a $1.776 billion fund for people who believe the government wronged them.

The settlement created a fund available to those claiming government mistreatment. The former judges contend this arrangement allowed the administration to avoid normal court procedures in resolving the president's dispute with the IRS. The bipartisan group filed their request with the court seeking judicial review of the settlement terms.

cards.headline: Court allows pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A federal appeals panel permitted Khalil to stay out of custody while he petitions the Supreme Court in his case against the Trump administration.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel allowed pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free as he takes his case against the Trump administration to the Supreme Court. Judges Stephanos Bibas, Arianna Freeman and Thomas Hardiman of the 3rd Circuit issued the decision.

The three-judge panel includes appointees of President Trump, former President George W. Bush and former President Joe Biden. Their ruling permits Khalil to avoid custody while pursuing his appeal to the nation's highest court.

cards.headline: Senator Andy Kim responds to criticism over ICE facility protest
cards.teaser: The New Jersey Democrat pushed back after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin criticized him for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility.
cards.body:
Senator Andy Kim fired back at Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after Mullin criticized the senator for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility in New Jersey. Mullin said during a Cabinet meeting at the White House that Kim complained about being hit by pepper ball spray at the protest.

Kim said the matter was never about him personally. The exchange followed Kim's participation in a demonstration outside the ICE facility in New Jersey, where he was among protesters exposed to pepper balls.

cards.headline: Senate Republican leaders move to reconcile with Ken Paxton after Texas primary
cards.teaser: GOP leadership is signaling to donors that maintaining the Senate majority requires unifying behind Paxton following his brutal primary against John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are working to repair their relationship with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following a contentious primary battle. The effort signals to major donors that maintaining Senate control depends on strong performance in Texas.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke with Paxton and subsequently endorsed him on a radio show. Republican leaders are moving past the divisive primary to present a unified front ahead of the general election.

cards.headline: Zelensky urges Trump and Congress to provide Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president asked for anti-missile defense systems, acknowledging Ukraine has not built its own production capability for such weapons.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and members of Congress to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia. Zelensky said Ukraine has achieved success in defending against drones but has not built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.
